analysis:
The supplied units are documentation-only: CHANGELOG.md head lines 1015-1426 (v0.10.9 through v0.10.13 candidate release notes). No executable source, build scripts or configuration changed in the visible evidence, so no control was weakened by these units. I examined them against the threat model for statements that could invalidate assumptions.

Items with security relevance, all described only as documentation and not verifiable here:
- The Me-first pause and local-first routing. Line 1171 says the local API stores the account key in memory, never in files or logs, and ignores client route headers. Line 1166 says `darkbloom route key` keeps the key in the Keychain. Lines 1255-1259 say the OpenCode and Hermes config writers never hold the key and back up files atomically. These relate to TB-003, A-008 and A-019; no implementation was supplied to check them.
- Busy-field and heartbeat semantics. Lines 1077-1078 say `draining` with `busy_reason: "owner"` is treated by coordinators as a plain drain. This is self-reported provider status related to A-018 and T-059 (TB-012); the coordinator handling is platform-owned and outside this evidence.
- Fixture downloader redirect restrictions (lines 1205-1221) are a build-time supply-chain hardening, not a regression.
- A 503 returned before SSE headers, and context-window clamping (lines 1053-1057). These are availability and input-validation behaviors related to T-010 and T-016. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the remaining new v0.10.13 text cannot be assessed.
- Update check retries (lines 1383-1386) and the claim that the registration and MLX pins are unchanged (line 1409 and the patch excerpt). I could not verify these from the supplied evidence. They touch TB-002 and T-054, but nothing in these units alters the attestation or authorization contract.

No prefix-cache (T-041), fan-helper, attestation or App Attest (TB-011) changes were observed. The remaining integration question is that the code behind these described behaviors (local API key handling, route passing, and Me-first pause) lives in other units not supplied here.
